chapter: Compositions, singers and the end of the big band
title: Billy Daniels
summary: Daniels sang at Dicky Wells' and joined the band for about two years, singing 'One Rose'.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: What about some of the vocalists like Billy Daniels and Della Reese and people like that?

Billy Daniels was working at one of the spots, (Inaudible), in Harlem during '34 when I first hit New York. It was Dicky Wells'. That's the spot. Tallulah Bankhead used to come up there a lot. There was, oh, you know, a lot of movie stars were downtown. He was working there and I was at the Ubanqi Club which was not too far from Dicky Wells'. Billy was singing there. He comes to the Concorde up here and tells his story on the stage a lot. So, somebody down there said the band, the 'Bama State Collegians with Erskine Hawkins needs a singer down there. Why don't you go down there and try out for him, or something like that. So, Billy did and I gave him a chance. And, he started singing with me then cause he was just going into Dicky Wells' just to sing off and on. So, after that, he turned out to be my band's singer along with Jimmy Mitchelle and I goes into the Apollo Theater. And, the tune I had for Billy to sing on the stage was "One Rose". Now, that was a waltz. The first time we ever did that on stage, a waltz, and the

first time they had a waltz sung in the Apollo Theater cause that was a jumping theater there. So, he went over very big. And Billy was with me for about, maybe about 2 years, with me as my band singer.
And right now, he comes up here all the time to do his singing. He comes in the lounge and we have a ball. We talk about those years. Yeah, good times.
Did he have the same kind of style then with using his body as he does in things like "Black Magic" and all like that?
Right. Yeah. That came along. Oh, he was gonna set a standard of straight up singing. And looked good, you know?
